title: Workflow: concurrent sd create calls lose seeds (advisory-lock RMW race)
description: Two agents calling sd create in the same second both read-modify-write .seeds/issues.jsonl under the advisory lock; last writer wins, silently dropping the other's issue. Cost us 13 seeds in one collision (2026-08-13). Fix ideas: per-create uuid pre-claim + merge, or a short retry on file-change detection, or a locked batch-append API. Visible to all agents via sd list; risk grows with more concurrent agents (GATE-R1-COORD two-agent workflow).

title: CAUTION: trace_rtl_cell loss numbers are a misconfigured-cell artifact
description: Laura's read-only audit of /var/tmp/opencode/trace_rtl_cell (2026-08-13 evening): the 3.3%/168-flit-loss and late-trace conclusions are NOT trustworthy evidence. Facts: (1) trace.txt has ALL 128 sources, not the intended 4 (trace_matrix_4src.mat does not exist — matrix traffic was never applied; trace is 128-src all-to-all with num_vcs=1); (2) binary vbuild_2die was built -GVCS=2 (1-VC convention) against a cfg with num_vcs=4 then overridden to 1 — mismatch; (3) binary predates the B->A route2d fix. Result: RTL delivered only 54/5038 pids (~99% loss, uniform across all 128 srcs) — a misconfig artifact, NOT an RTL flit-loss bug. rtl_flits.txt line 4721 is a truncated dump ('7742 0 2'), a symptom not the cause. Real next step: build the cell correctly (4-src matrix actually applied, num_vcs matching binary, post-B->A-fix binary) before drawing any loss conclusion. B->A routing gap itself is REAL (Dave's code reading is correct) — keep that fix. Do not close the trace epic until a correctly-built cell runs.
